newsitem.title: USA: Shuttle Discovery heads for Florida.
newsitem.headline: Shuttle Discovery heads for Florida.

text.p: Space shuttle Discovery headed for a rare nighttime touchdown early on Friday after a 10-day mission to refurbish the Hubble Space Telescope.
Mission commander Ken Bowersox and copilot Scott Horowitz fired Discovery's braking rockets at 2:22 a.m. EST (0722 GMT) to begin a one-hour, 10-minute descent through the atmosphere.
Touchdown on the flood-lit runway at Florida's Kennedy Space Centre was scheduled for 3:32 a.m. EST (0832 GMT).

The shuttle was kept in space for one more orbit of the earth due to cloudy conditions at the Florida spaceport. Flight controllers looked at diverting the shuttle to its backup landing strip in California, but the skies in Florida cleared in time for its second landing opportunity.
Discovery's planned nighttime landing would be only the ninth in the 82-flight shuttle programme.
The recent installation of 52 Halogen lights down the centre of the runway would help Bowersox keep the gliding shuttle lined up for a perfect touchdown, NASA officials said.
The shuttle touches down at nearly twice the speed of a conventional airliner and there is little room for error. The space centre runway is surrounded by ditches and alligator-infested swamps.
Nighttime and low-light dawn landings were expected to become more commonplace when NASA begins assembly of its international space station.

Discovery blasted off from the Kennedy Space Centre before dawn on Feb. 11. Two teams of spacewalking astronauts spent 33 hours outside to refurbish and upgrade the $2 billion orbiting observatory. They installed two new instruments and eight other upgraded compartments.
